title: Quotient formula for extension along an invertible scalar map
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a symmetric monoidal closed category with equalizers and coequalizers, in which tensoring on either side preserves colimits. Let $R,S$ be commutative monoid objects ([sk-def-sfb-ring-object]) and $\varphi:R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ an isomorphism of monoid objects. Module objects and their morphisms are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use restriction, extension and coextension of scalars as in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For an $R$-module $N$ with action $\gamma_N:R\otimes N\to N$, put $T_N=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}N$; its underlying object is $N$ and its $S$-action is $\beta_N=\gamma_N\circ(\varphi^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)$. Write $\eta_S:\mathbf1\to S$ for the unit and $\lambda_A:\mathbf1\otimes A\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ for the left unitor.

Let $F_N=\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}N=S\otimes_R N$, with coequalizer map $q_N:S\otimes N\to F_N$. The action $\beta_N$ coequalizes the two maps defining $F_N$. The component $p_N:F_N\xrightarrow{\sim}T_N$ of the adjoint-uniqueness comparison of [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso] is the unique factor satisfying
$$p_N\circ q_N=\beta_N.$$
Its inverse has underlying morphism
$$s_N=q_N\circ(\eta_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)\circ\lambda_N^{-1}:N\to F_N.$$
With the $S$-action of $T_N$ on the domain of $s_N$, both $p_N$ and $s_N$ are $S$-linear, and
$$p_N\circ s_N=\mathrm{id}_{T_N},\qquad s_N\circ p_N=\mathrm{id}_{F_N}.$$
The $p_N$ and $s_N$ are natural in $R$-module morphisms $N\to N'$. Thus the extension comparison is normalized by its value on the coequalizer map, and its inverse is insertion of the unit followed by that coequalizer map.

proof.text: Use the specified comparison p = extendScalarsIsoComapInv, which is defined by left-adjoint uniqueness for the extension-restriction adjunction and the adjunction of the inverse restriction equivalence. The Mathlib equation homEquiv_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app identifies the image of p_N with the unit of the latter adjunction. Its underlying arrow is the identity: the inverse equivalence unit is the inverse of the original counit, and that counit is composed of comapComp, comapCongr and comapId, all with identity underlying arrows. Unfolding the extension Hom equivalence therefore gives u_N followed by p_N equal to the identity.

The extension API already proves that tensoring unit insertion u_N with S and then applying the extension action a_F gives q_N (whiskerLeft_extendUnitHom_smul'). Since p_N is a module morphism, a_F followed by p_N equals S tensor p_N followed by the inverse-restriction action beta_N. Thus q_N followed by p_N equals S tensor (u_N followed by p_N) followed by beta_N, hence equals beta_N by step 1. Postcompose the defining coequalizer equation for q_N with p_N to obtain the claimed coequalizing equation for beta_N. If another underlying arrow f has q_N followed by f equal to beta_N, cancellation of the epimorphism q_N gives f = p_N.

Since p_N is an isomorphism, cancel it from u_N followed by p_N equal to the identity to identify u_N with the underlying arrow of the inverse comparison. This proves the asserted inverse formula, its S-linearity, and the second inverse identity; the first inverse identity is step 1. All use the component isomorphism and the faithful forgetful functor on module objects.

Naturality of the comparison as a natural transformation gives the forward naturality equation after taking underlying arrows. Naturality of its inverse gives the inverse equation after replacing each inverse component by u_N using step 3. Restriction of scalars keeps the underlying arrows unchanged.
